Contributing guidelines

  • I have read CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

Module(s)

mini.completion, mini.snippets

Question

I'm in the middle of a migration from neovim 0.6 with a set of vimscript plugins to neovim 0.12 with a MiniMax setup. One issue I've stumbled upon is using auto-import in Typescript using mini.completion with TS LSP.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open main.tsx from vitejs' example app.
  2. Delete existing import { StrictMode } from "react";
  3. Enter insert mode, start typing import strictmode
  4. First element in the completion menu suggested by LSP is called Variable, by it's an auto-import.
  5. Press <C-n> to select.
  6. Text import { StrictMode$1 } from "react"; is inserted into current line.

7a. If I press <Esc>, the text is kept as is, leaving the code in the incorrect state (notice the "$1" after the StrictMode).

7b. If I press <CR>instead, the editor switches into mini.snippets mode with cursor being positioned after the StrictMode (and another jump spot is suggested at the end)

Pressing <Esc> again, and I have the correctly imported line, although with a missing space at the end. Not a real issue if you have a formatter set up.

7c. If I press <C-y> instead (to be honest, I have never heard of this binding 😳 , but spotted it in another LSP related discussion here), then I get the same snippets mode. Finally, if I press <Esc>, then I get a fully correct import

Am I doing something wrong?

My question is, can I get a behavior similar to coc.nvim autocompletion, where I only needed to
type import strictmode, then press <Esc> (or <Space>) to get the correct line? It has less keystrokes, after all.

Or, if the <C-y><Esc> combination is the only correct way to do this, should we mention it in the MiniMax comments related to mini.completion plugin? (the whole commentary on MiniMax is epic btw!)

Also, it could be another issue with LSP misbehaving like in the previous reports, but I'm not sure here.

Set up test environment
  1. Using neovim 0.12
  2. Fresh install MiniMax
  3. Using NodeJS 22+
  4. Set up a test app with npm create vite@latest. Accept React, then Typescript.
  5. In the MiniMax config, uncomment Mason, install it, then install "typescript-language-server" via Mason.
  6. In the MiniMax config, uncomment vim.lsp.enable and add ts_ls.
  7. Open src/main.tsx from the test app.

comment_data.body:
I didn't reproduce the exact case with exact completion candidate, but I am fairly certain this is a regular "How to handle snippet candidates?" situation. As the `StrictMode` candidate is a snippet (there is an `S` label to its right). Here are relevant parts of documentation:

- The ['mini.completion' part](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-completion.html#module-snippets). This rules out the "7a. Immediate `<Esc>`" approach. Snippet candidates need to be explicitly accepted: either with `<C-y>` (a standard way of accepting a candidate in built-in Insert mode completion; `:h complete_CTRL-Y`) or by typing non-keyword character (like `<Space>`). I prefer the second approach since it allows "just keep typing what you intended" workflow.
- After accepting a snippet, [it is inserted](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-completion.html#minicompletion.default_snippet_insert) and it is "... expected to navigate/jump between dedicated places (tabstops) to adjust inserted text as needed". In this particular case the `$1` is a first tabstop that snippet provider thinks might be adjusted. If you don't want/need to do that, jump to the next tabstop which in this case is a final one at the end (you can see different inline symbols for them). Now either exiting into the Normal mode or keeping typing will automatically stop the snippet session.

    An alternative to "jump through all tabstops" is an explicit stop of snippet session via `<C-c>`.

    All this is described in how ['mini.snippets' handles snippet session](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-snippets.html#minisnippets.default_insert-sessionlifecycle).

> Or, if the `<C-y><Esc>` combination is the only correct way to do this, should we mention it in the MiniMax comments related to mini.completion plugin?

The general idea is described in the MiniMax annotation comments already: [one](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/8135af233210ecd7916516f35602e220874ea2df/configs/nvim-0.12/plugin/30_mini.lua#L149-L150), [two](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/8135af233210ecd7916516f35602e220874ea2df/configs/nvim-0.12/plugin/30_mini.lua#L162-L163), [three](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/8135af233210ecd7916516f35602e220874ea2df/configs/nvim-0.12/plugin/30_mini.lua#L698-L709). There is only so much these comments can fit to not start being intimidating.

> (the whole commentary on MiniMax is epic btw!)

Thanks, it took a lot of effort :pray:

reply_data.body:
Really appreciate the meticulous answer! ❤️ 

Given that I didn't plan to use snippets _via LSP_ (I do use mini.snippets, but they are activated with a separate binding in my config), and therefore the only snippets I'd get was such imports, I hacked the `snippet_insert` to save an extra key, so that I only had to type `<C-n><C-y>` in most cases:

```lua
local snippet_insert = function(snippet)
  vim.snippet.expand(snippet)
  vim.cmd('stopinsert')
end

require('mini.completion').setup({
  lsp_completion = {
    -- usual MiniMax setup ...
    snippet_insert = snippet_insert,
  },
})

```

> There is only so much these comments can fit to not start being intimidating.

I swear I was reading them as a good book. Neo/vim has a pretty good documentation, but I always felt intimidated by the number of options and a specific language there. Your explanations are much closer to an average person. So please, don't underestimate the educational importance of MiniMax comments ☝🏻

reply_data.body:
> I hacked the `snippet_insert` to save an extra key, so that I only had to type `<C-n><C-y>` in most cases:

This is not really a good way to handle this. The problem is that this will leave cursor at the first tabstop which often not the one snippet author intended as the "final place to keep cursor". And automatically exiting into a Normal mode after accepting a snippet breaks the typing flow.

My honest suggestion would be try to get accustomed to using snippets whenever they are presented. The 'mini.snippets' module provides more streamlined snippet session behavior with more feedback.

If you still don't want that, I would suggest using `MiniCompletion.default_snippet_insert(snippet)` instead of `vim.snippet.expand(snippet)`. It will use 'mini.snippets' in a correct way. To stop the snippet session, add an extra `MiniSnippets.session.stop()` call after inserting a snippet.

A (presumably) more robust way of handling this would be to ask an LSP server to not provide snippets. This is done by adjusting [advertised capabilities](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/8135af233210ecd7916516f35602e220874ea2df/configs/nvim-0.12/plugin/30_mini.lua#L190). With something like this:

```lua
local capabilities = MiniCompletion.get_lsp_capabilities()
capabilities.textDocument.completion.completionItem.snippetSupport = false
vim.lsp.config('*', { capabilities = capabilities })
```

This should work in theory (if I did set correct capability).

reply_data.body:
> The problem is that this will leave cursor at the first tabstop which often not the one snippet author intended as the "final place to keep cursor". And automatically exiting into a Normal mode after accepting a snippet breaks the typing flow

This is all true for a general snippet case. But here I assume that the only snippet I will get is the `import` one. For them the typical scenario for me is:

1. I realize I've used new local variable from another module.
2. Move to the file top.
3. Introduce a new `import` line.
4. Jump back to the file editing somewhere in the middle.

Therefore in 95% cases I don't need to edit the line. I simply want it to be inserted there as is, and switching to normal mode is a part of the process. 

~~I wish there was some kind of auto-importing plugin that would do that for me in background, but I could not find any plugin for that.~~ I just realized there's a thing called "actions" in LSP! I can put the cursor on the new local var, type `<Leader>la` and choose "Add import from "react"! w00t! I feel so releived and embarassed at the same time 😅
